programs.name: MCPA Certification Curriculum
programs.summary: A free, open-source path to the Model Context Protocol Associate exam, built by implementing MCP hosts, clients, servers, and tools against the 2026-07-28 specification.
programs.promise: Learn the judgment the exam measures by building the protocol the exam describes.
programs.accessNotice: As verified on September 24, 2026, the MCPA exam is open enrollment through Linux Foundation Training and Certification. This open curriculum is available to everyone. Verify current pricing, format, and eligibility on the official page before scheduling, because program details can change.
programs.disclaimer: This is an independent community curriculum. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, sponsored by, or authorized by the Agentic AI Foundation or the Linux Foundation. It does not contain live exam questions. The official exam page and current program policies always take precedence.
programs.scoringNotice: Practice percentages in this curriculum are raw scores over original questions. The official passing score and scoring scale for the MCPA are not published, so practice results cannot predict an official outcome.
programs.sourcePolicy: Every exam fact is mapped to the official MCPA certification page and the launch announcement, with the retrieval date recorded in research/source-verification-ledger.md. Protocol facts are mapped to the MCP 2026-07-28 specification. Lessons and questions are original.

tracks.summary: Prove you understand how the Model Context Protocol works: its hosts, clients, servers, and tools, the message flow and primitives that connect them, and the trust boundaries that keep the connection safe.
tracks.audience: AI engineers, platform engineers, and AI governance professionals who connect agents to external systems and need to reason about how the protocol works and how its components communicate.
recommendedExperience: Foundational knowledge of JSON-RPC or a similar message-based protocol
Experience calling LLM APIs such as OpenAI, Anthropic, or a local model
Understanding of agentic patterns such as tool use and the think-act-observe loop
Basic security literacy: API keys, OAuth 2.1, token handling, and authentication headers
Ability to read an MCP server manifest and its capability definitions

domains.name: MCP Fundamentals
objectives: Explain the purpose and scope of MCP and the integration problem it standardizes between AI applications and external systems
Describe the core MCP concepts of hosts, clients, servers, primitives, and the stateless JSON-RPC request model
Reason about interoperability, protocol versioning, and the value of one open protocol over per-system custom integrations
Read the MCP specification, its revision history, and its feature lifecycle to tell current, deprecated, and removed behavior apart

domains.name: Architecture and Components
objectives: Read the schemas and structured data that define MCP messages, tool definitions, capabilities, and server manifests
Distinguish the responsibilities of MCP hosts, clients, and servers and how discovery and capability negotiation connect them
Trace the model interaction flow from a user request through the host, model, client, and server and back into model context

domains.name: Interactions and Execution
objectives: Apply the request, notification, subscription, and multi round-trip interaction patterns and handle each result type
Handle protocol errors and tool execution errors, including version, capability, header, and validation failures
Walk the tool invocation lifecycle from discovery and selection through call, user input, progress, cancellation, and result
Identify the protocol primitives and utilities, including tools, resources, prompts, completion, caching, pagination, transports, and deprecated client features

domains.name: Security and Governance
objectives: Locate the trust boundaries between host, client, server, model, and the tools and content a server exposes
Apply OAuth-based authorization, client registration, scopes, and user consent so a user approves what a server may see and do
Choose risk and safety controls against tool poisoning, injection, token misuse, and over-broad access
Design auditability and observability so protocol activity can be traced, attributed, and reviewed

domains.name: Use Cases and Ecosystem
objectives: Map the roles, responsibilities, governance, and adoption patterns of teams building and deploying MCP
Select operational use cases and the primitives or extensions that fit each one
Reason about ecosystem portability across clients, servers, SDKs, extensions, gateways, and registries
